questions.q: State the order of the differential equation $y'' + 3y' - 2y = \sin x$.
questions.answer: Second order (the highest derivative appearing is $y''$).

questions.q: Verify that $y = e^{2x}$ is a solution of $y' - 2y = 0$.
questions.answer: $y' = 2e^{2x}$, so $y' - 2y = 2e^{2x} - 2e^{2x} = 0$. Yes, it is a solution.
Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = x\,dx$. Integrate: $\ln|y| = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + C$. So $y = Ae^{x^2/2}$.
Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y^2} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $-\dfrac{1}{y} = \ln x + C$. So $y = \dfrac{-1}{\ln x + C}$.
$\dfrac{dy}{y} = 3x^2\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = x^3 + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{x^3}$. Since $y(0)=2$, $A=2$: $y = 2e^{x^3}$.
$\dfrac{dy}{y} = -2x\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = -x^2 + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{-x^2}$. Since $y(0)=5$, $A=5$: $y = 5e^{-x^2}$.

sections.heading: Application: radioactive decay and population growth

questions.q: A radioactive substance decays according to $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -kA$. If $A(0) = 100$ g and $A(5) = 50$ g, find $k$.
questions.answer: $A = 100e^{-kt}$. Then $50 = 100e^{-5k} \Rightarrow e^{-5k} = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow -5k = \ln\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{\ln 2}{5} \approx 0.1386$ per unit time.

questions.q: A population grows according to $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 0.03P$, with $P(0) = 200$. Find $P(10)$.

questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{1+y^2} = \dfrac{dx}{1+x^2}$. Integrate: $\arctan y = \arctan x + C$.
$\dfrac{dy}{y} = \cos x\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = \sin x + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{\sin x}$. Since $y(0)=1$, $A=1$: $y = e^{\sin x}$.
$y\,dy = x^2\,dx \Rightarrow \dfrac{y^2}{2} = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + C \Rightarrow y^2 = \dfrac{2}{3}x^3 + C'$.
Rewrite as $e^y\,dy = e^x\,dx$. Integrate: $e^y = e^x + C$, so $y = \ln(e^x+C)$.

sections.heading: A separable equation solved via partial fractions

questions.answer: $\int\left(\dfrac{1}{y}+\dfrac{1}{1-y}\right)dy = \int dx \Rightarrow \ln|y|-\ln|1-y| = x+C \Rightarrow \ln\left|\dfrac{y}{1-y}\right|=x+C$. So $\dfrac{y}{1-y}=Ae^x$, giving $y = \dfrac{Ae^x}{1+Ae^x}$.
$\dfrac{dy}{y^2}=2x\,dx \Rightarrow -\dfrac{1}{y}=x^2+C \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{-1}{x^2+C}$. Since $y(0)=1$, $C=-1$: $y = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2}$.

questions.q: For $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x-y$, what does the slope field look like along the line $y=x$?
questions.answer: Along $y=x$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x-x=0$, so every slope-field arrow on that line is horizontal.

questions.q: For $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^2$, explain why any solution with $y(0)>0$ must be increasing for as long as it's defined.
questions.answer: $y^2 \geq 0$ always, and $y^2>0$ whenever $y\ne0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}\geq0$ everywhere the solution is defined — a solution that starts positive never decreases.

sections.heading: Verifying a solution to an applied model

questions.q: Newton's Law of Cooling states $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_{\text{room}})$. Verify that $T(t)=T_{\text{room}}+(T_0-T_{\text{room}})e^{-kt}$ solves it.
questions.answer: $T'(t) = -k(T_0-T_{\text{room}})e^{-kt}$. Since $T(t)-T_{\text{room}} = (T_0-T_{\text{room}})e^{-kt}$, this equals $-k(T(t)-T_{\text{room}})$, matching the equation.

questions.q: A cup of coffee at $90^\circ$C is placed in a $20^\circ$C room. Newton's Law of Cooling gives $T(t)=20+70e^{-kt}$. If the coffee cools to $70^\circ$C after 10 minutes, find $k$.
questions.answer: $70=20+70e^{-10k} \Rightarrow 50=70e^{-10k} \Rightarrow e^{-10k}=\dfrac{5}{7} \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{\ln(7/5)}{10} \approx 0.0336$ per minute.

sections.heading: One more round of separable-equation practice

questions.answer: $y\,dy=(x+1)\,dx \Rightarrow \dfrac{y^2}{2}=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x+C \Rightarrow y^2=x^2+2x+2C$. Using $y(1)=2$: $4=1+2+2C \Rightarrow 2C=1$, so $y^2=x^2+2x+1=(x+1)^2$, giving $y=x+1$ (taking the branch matching $y(1)=2$).
$\dfrac{dy}{y}=\dfrac{dx}{x+1} \Rightarrow \ln|y|=\ln|x+1|+C \Rightarrow y=A(x+1)$.

sections.heading: A final pair of separable equations

questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{y}=\dfrac{dx}{x} \Rightarrow \ln|y|=\ln x+C \Rightarrow y=Ax$.
$\dfrac{dy}{y}=3\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y|=3x+C \Rightarrow y=Ae^{3x}$. Since $y(0)=4$, $A=4$: $y=4e^{3x}$.
